Amumu.watch: Amumu Q Bandage Toss stuns you and lets him close the gap, so move with jungle monsters or minions between you and him. Amumu R Curse of the Sad Mummy stuns enemies in an area, so keep your distance before Amumu gets close and avoid grouping with allies. Amumu W Despair keeps dealing damage based on your maximum health while you remain close, so don’t stay near him for long.
Amumu.build: Use Null-Magic Mantle to hold on early and choose Mercury’s Treads. Amumu deals mostly magic damage, so build magic resistance first. If Amumu’s crowd control often catches an allied carry, fit Mikael’s Blessing between your core items.
Amumu.fight: Use Ivern Q Rootcaller to root Amumu and help allies engage, and use Ivern E Triggerseed on allies going in to protect them. While Amumu Q Bandage Toss and Amumu R Curse of the Sad Mummy are available, don’t recast Ivern Q Rootcaller to dive in first.
Amumu.laning: Use Ivern P Friend of the Forest to seed several camps in advance, then visit lanes to gank while they grow. When an ally is ready to follow up, hit Ivern Q Rootcaller and use Ivern E Triggerseed to help them engage.
Amumu.combo: When your allies are ready to engage, root Amumu with Ivern Q Rootcaller and use Ivern E Triggerseed on an ally going in so its slow follows as the root ends. Recast Ivern Q Rootcaller to follow only when needed. If you summon Ivern R Daisy!, command her to keep attacking Amumu, and look for an area slow when you can use Ivern E Triggerseed on Daisy.
Amumu.escape: After Amumu Q Bandage Toss or Amumu R Curse of the Sad Mummy is used, look for a chance to catch him with Ivern Q Rootcaller. Amumu has no ability to create distance on his own, so chain roots with your allies and recast Ivern Q Rootcaller to engage if needed. If Amumu still has crowd control available, Ivern should stay back and keep his distance.
Amumu.teamfight: Start from behind, and space out from allies so Amumu R Curse of the Sad Mummy doesn’t catch several of you. Position Ivern R Daisy! between an allied carry and Amumu to block Amumu Q Bandage Toss, and use Ivern E Triggerseed when Amumu engages and reaches the carry. After Amumu R Curse of the Sad Mummy is used, catch him with Ivern Q Rootcaller to give your allies a chance to fight.
Amumu.phase: In the mid and late game, Ivern should protect allied carries and stop Amumu from engaging instead of leading the fight.

Brand.watch: Brand P Blaze stacks when you’re hit by spells in succession, then explodes, so dodge his first spell. In particular, Brand Q Sear stuns you if you’re ablaze, so dodge the projectile or stand behind minions. Also walk out of the marked area for Brand W Pillar of Flame immediately.
Brand.build: In the early game, buy Null-Magic Mantle first and choose Mercury’s Treads for boots. Brand deals mostly magic damage, and Ivern has relatively low magic resistance, so build magic resistance first. Brand P Blaze deals damage based on maximum health, so avoid choices that only add health.
Brand.fight: As soon as Brand W Pillar of Flame is used, root Brand with Ivern Q Rootcaller if your allies are ready to engage. Brand has no mobility abilities, so pressure him with Ivern R Daisy! once you close the gap.
Brand.laning: Use Ivern P Friend of the Forest to seed several camps, then visit a lane and try to gank while they grow. If Brand has set the minion wave on fire, approach from the side and avoid standing next to burning minions.
Brand.combo: When your allies are ready to engage, hit Ivern Q Rootcaller and use Ivern E Triggerseed on an ally a little early so its slow follows as the root ends. Then summon Ivern R Daisy! and command her to keep attacking Brand; use E on Daisy too to look for an area slow. If Daisy keeps attacking the same target, her third attack knocks them up.
Brand.escape: Go in when Brand W Pillar of Flame is down and your allies are ready to engage. If you’re ablaze, Brand Q Sear can stun you, so dodge the projectile first or wait for the fire to go out. Then root Brand with Ivern Q Rootcaller and close the gap.
Brand.phase: In the mid and late game, focus on saving allied carries and stopping the enemy engage.
Brand.teamfight: Brand E Conflagration and Brand R Pyroclasm can spread or bounce between allies, so don’t stand near an ally who is burning. Stay back and catch Brand with Ivern Q Rootcaller so your allies can engage him, and use Ivern E Triggerseed when an allied carry is taking damage. Position Ivern R Daisy! in front of the carry to block skillshots, then send her along Brand’s escape route to look for a knock-up when Brand falters.

Briar.watch: Briar Q Head Rush stuns and lowers armor and magic resistance, so keep your distance to avoid it. When Briar charges E Chilling Scream, don’t stand with your back to a wall, and look for a chance to interrupt the charge with Daisy’s knock-up. Briar R Certain Death chases the first champion it hits until the end, so stand behind your frontline.
Briar.build: Build armor first to deal with Briar’s main source of damage. Briar E Chilling Scream and Briar R Certain Death deal magic damage, so armor alone won’t stop them. If an allied carry is often caught by crowd control, consider fitting Mikael’s Blessing between your core items, since Ivern E Triggerseed can’t remove it.
Briar.fight: When Briar engages, catch her with Ivern Q Rootcaller and protect the ally she’s attacking with Ivern E Triggerseed. If the fight is likely to go long and let Briar heal, consider Grievous Wounds after building resistances.
Briar.laning: Seed camps early, then move to an allied lane and look for a gank with Ivern Q Rootcaller. Ward against Briar’s early ganks and reckless engages, and don’t stay long in the middle of a lane without vision. Avoid routes where you might run into Briar and move toward lanes with allies.
Briar.combo: When your allies are ready to engage, root Briar with Ivern Q Rootcaller and use Ivern E Triggerseed on an ally going in so its slow follows as the root ends. Recast Ivern Q Rootcaller to engage with them only when needed. If you summon Ivern R Daisy!, command her to keep attacking Briar and use Ivern E Triggerseed on Daisy to look for an area slow.
Briar.escape: Don’t go in just because Briar Q Head Rush is down. Briar W Blood Frenzy / Snack Attack and Briar R Certain Death can also be used to engage, so look especially for a window before Briar R Certain Death comes back up. Then catch her with Ivern Q Rootcaller alongside your allies and send in Ivern R Daisy!.
Briar.phase: In the mid and late game, focus on saving allied carries and stopping Briar’s engage.
Briar.teamfight: Start from behind and catch Briar with Ivern Q Rootcaller; use Ivern E Triggerseed as soon as she reaches an allied carry. Take advantage of Briar in W Blood Frenzy charging at the nearest enemy by positioning your frontline and Daisy in front of the carry. When Briar charges E Chilling Scream, look for a chance to interrupt it with Daisy’s knock-up.

Elise.watch: When Elise transforms with Elise R Spider Form after health has dropped, she is looking for a finishing blow, so be ready to use Ivern E Triggerseed.
Elise.build: Early on, buy a Null-Magic Mantle first and choose Mercury's Treads for boots. Elise’s damage is mostly magic, and the stun from Elise E Cocoon is also dangerous, so prioritize magic resistance and tenacity.
Elise.fight: Right after Elise uses Elise Q Neurotoxin / Venomous Bite, catch her with Ivern Q Rootcaller. While your allies close in, protect them with Ivern E Triggerseed.
Elise.laning: Early on, keep plenty of vision and don’t push your lane recklessly when Elise is missing. Use Ivern P Friend of the Forest to prepare camps in advance, then try to gank a lane and return to collect them while they grow.
Elise.combo: When your allies are ready to follow up, hit Elise with Ivern Q Rootcaller and shield an ally with Ivern E Triggerseed so its slow continues after the root ends. Recast Ivern Q Rootcaller to engage if needed. If you summon Ivern R Daisy!, direct her to keep attacking the same target and apply Ivern E Triggerseed to Daisy.
Elise.escape: After confirming that both Elise E Cocoon and Elise E Rappel have been fully used, counter-engage with your allies. Also look for a chance to catch Elise with Ivern Q Rootcaller right after she uses Elise Q Neurotoxin / Venomous Bite.
Elise.phase: Early on, watch for Elise’s ganks and keep vision so you don’t give up kills. If you prevent her from gaining an early lead and stall the game, the matchup improves; in the mid and late game, keep your allied carries alive and stop her engages.
Elise.teamfight: Start from the back and catch an enemy with Ivern Q Rootcaller so your allies can attack. When Elise engages on an allied carry, shield them with Ivern E Triggerseed and place Ivern R Daisy! in front of the carry to block skillshots. If crowd control like Elise E Cocoon keeps locking down an allied carry, fit Mikael's Blessing in between your core items.

Ekko.watch: When you see the signal for Ekko W Parallel Convergence, leave the area to avoid the stun and shield. Watch which way Ekko Q Timewinder travels and dodge its return path too. When you see the afterimage from Ekko R Chronobreak, don’t chase recklessly, even when health is low.
Ekko.build: Build magic resistance first to defend against Ekko’s damage. Early on, rely on a Null-Magic Mantle and choose Mercury's Treads for boots.
Ekko.fight: Root Ekko with Ivern Q Rootcaller right after he closes in with Ekko E Phase Dive, creating an opening for your allies to attack. If Ekko R Chronobreak is ready, don’t chase deep solely because health is low.
Ekko.laning: Use Ivern P Friend of the Forest to plant brush at several jungle camps, then gank a lane while they grow. When your allies are ready to follow up, land Ivern Q Rootcaller to help them engage. Avoid paths where you might run into the enemy jungler alone and help the lanes where your allies are.
Ekko.combo: When your allies are ready to follow up, root Ekko with Ivern Q Rootcaller and shield the ally engaging with Ivern E Triggerseed. Time the shield so its explosion overlaps with the end of the root, and recast Ivern Q Rootcaller only when you also need to engage. If you summon Ivern R Daisy!, direct her to keep attacking Ekko and shield Daisy with Ivern E Triggerseed to apply the slow.
Ekko.escape: Right after Ekko closes in with Ekko E Phase Dive, root him with Ivern Q Rootcaller while his mobility is on cooldown. Start the main fight after both Ekko W Parallel Convergence and Ekko R Chronobreak are on cooldown. If only Ekko E Phase Dive is on cooldown, don’t go deep, since Ekko can escape with Ekko R Chronobreak.
Ekko.phase: In the mid and late game, focus on protecting your allied carries and stopping Ekko’s engages.
Ekko.teamfight: Start from the back. If Ekko uses Ekko E Phase Dive to reach a carry, root him with Ivern Q Rootcaller and shield the carry with Ivern E Triggerseed. Place Ivern R Daisy! in front of the carry to stop Ekko’s engage, and direct her to keep attacking the same target to look for a knock-up. When you see the signal for Ekko W Parallel Convergence, avoid its area, and look for a chance to attack after Ekko R Chronobreak is on cooldown.

Evelynn.watch: When you see the mark from Evelynn W Allure, warn your allies before the charm lands and retreat toward an area with vision.
Evelynn.build: Early on, buy a Null-Magic Mantle first and choose Mercury's Treads for boots. Prioritize magic resistance against Evelynn’s main damage, but focus first on retreating before the mark from Evelynn W Allure matures.
Evelynn.fight: When your allies are ready to follow up, root Evelynn with Ivern Q Rootcaller and shield the ally engaging with Ivern E Triggerseed to chain the shield and slow.
Evelynn.laning: Use Ivern P Friend of the Forest to plant brush at camps and try to gank lanes while it grows. Place vision beside camps where Evelynn might start a fight and along her gank paths.
Evelynn.combo: When your allies are ready to follow up, hit Evelynn with Ivern Q Rootcaller and shield the engaging ally with Ivern E Triggerseed a little early so the slow continues when the root ends. Recast Ivern Q Rootcaller to engage with them if needed. If you summon Ivern R Daisy!, direct her to keep attacking Evelynn and shield Daisy with Ivern E Triggerseed.
Evelynn.escape: If only Evelynn E Whiplash is on cooldown, don’t engage hastily, since she can escape with Evelynn R Last Caress. Before Evelynn R Last Caress comes back, close the distance with Ivern Q Rootcaller alongside your allies and use Ivern R Daisy! to catch her.
Evelynn.phase: In the mid and late game, focus on protecting your allied carries and stopping Evelynn’s engages.
Evelynn.teamfight: Start from the back and help your damage dealers stay inside an area with vision. If Evelynn gets into your back line, shield the carry with Ivern E Triggerseed and catch Evelynn with Ivern Q Rootcaller and Ivern R Daisy!’s knock-up. Keep Daisy in front of the carry and direct her to keep attacking the same target.

Graves.watch: Graves Q End of the Line explodes immediately when it hits a wall, so don’t fight with your back to a wall or in a narrow jungle passage. If you’re caught in Graves W Smoke Screen, your vision is blocked and you’re slowed, so leave the area by the shortest route. Graves P New Destiny’s basic attack damage is blocked by the first unit hit, so fight with an ally or Ivern R Daisy! between you and Graves.
Graves.build: Graves deals mostly physical damage, so build armor first and get Plated Steelcaps early. Armor can’t block the magic damage from Graves W Smoke Screen.
Graves.fight: Catch Graves with Ivern Q Rootcaller while he reloads after firing two shots to help your allies engage. Fight in open terrain where there’s room to dodge the explosion from Graves Q End of the Line.
Graves.laning: Early on, plant seeds at several camps with Ivern P Friend of the Forest and try to gank lanes while they grow. When your allies are ready to follow up, hit Graves with Ivern Q Rootcaller to pressure him. Avoid paths where you might run into Graves in the enemy jungle and move toward your allied lanes.
Graves.combo: When your allies are ready to follow up, root Graves with Ivern Q Rootcaller and shield the engaging ally with Ivern E Triggerseed. Time the explosion from Ivern E Triggerseed to overlap with the end of the root, and recast Ivern Q Rootcaller to join in if needed. If you summon Ivern R Daisy!, direct her to keep attacking Graves and shield Daisy with Ivern E Triggerseed.
Graves.escape: Even if Graves E Quickdraw is on cooldown, he can still escape if Graves R Collateral Damage is available. In particular, before Graves R Collateral Damage comes back, close the distance with Ivern Q Rootcaller and send Ivern R Daisy! in when your allies can engage with you.
Graves.phase: Graves gets stronger over time, making the matchup harder, so focus on protecting your allied carries in the mid and late game.
Graves.teamfight: Start from the back and catch Graves with Ivern Q Rootcaller so your allies can attack. If Graves goes for an allied carry, use Ivern E Triggerseed on the carry and place Ivern R Daisy! in front to block his path. Cast Ivern W Brushmaker in your team’s area just before a team fight to gain empowered basic attacks and a vision advantage.

Fiddlesticks.watch: Fiddlesticks R Crowstorm moves after channeling, so interrupt it with Ivern Q Rootcaller or Ivern R Daisy! when you see it being cast. If you cannot interrupt it, move out of range. When Fiddlesticks has been missing for a while, watch bushes without vision and narrow entrances. Fiddlesticks E Reap silences if it hits the center, so avoid the middle of your formation.
Fiddlesticks.build: Early on, first rely on a Null-Magic Mantle to survive, and choose Mercury's Treads for boots. Since Fiddlesticks deals mostly magic damage and Ivern has relatively low magic resistance, build magic resistance first.
Fiddlesticks.fight: If Fiddlesticks comes in with R Crowstorm, leave its range, then focus your damage with your allies to counterattack.
Fiddlesticks.laning: Plant Friend of the Forest groves at several camps, then gank lanes while they grow. When your ally is ready to follow up, hit Ivern Q Rootcaller to help them engage. Keep the bushes behind your lanes warded against Fiddlesticks's ambushes from outside your vision, and do not pass by an unchecked Scarecrow Effigy.
Fiddlesticks.combo: When your ally is ready to follow up, hit Ivern Q Rootcaller, then cast Ivern E Triggerseed on that ally as they engage. Cast Ivern E Triggerseed a little early so its explosion coincides with the root ending, and recast Ivern Q Rootcaller to go in only when needed. If you summon Ivern R Daisy!, command her to keep attacking the same target and apply Ivern E Triggerseed to her to aim for an area slow and knock-up.
Fiddlesticks.escape: Once Fiddlesticks Q Terrify and Fiddlesticks E Reap are down, the risk of being locked down by fear and silence is lower.
Fiddlesticks.teamfight: Before a team fight, spread out and secure vision in the bushes and entrances near the objective to prevent an ambush with Fiddlesticks R Crowstorm. From behind, catch one enemy with Ivern Q Rootcaller, and cast Ivern E Triggerseed if Fiddlesticks goes on an allied carry. Place Ivern R Daisy! in front of your carry to stop the engage, and look for a chance to interrupt Fiddlesticks W Bountiful Harvest's channel.
Fiddlesticks.phase: In the mid and late game, Ivern should protect allied carries and stop engages instead of taking the frontline.

Gragas.watch: When you see Gragas Q Barrel Roll, leave its radius before it explodes. If you counterattack where Gragas E Body Slam hits you, you are likely to get hit by R Explosive Cask too, so get away first. When Gragas has R Explosive Cask available, do not stand with your back to the enemy team.
Gragas.build: Early on, first rely on a Null-Magic Mantle to survive, and choose Mercury's Treads for boots. Since Gragas deals mostly magic damage and Ivern has relatively low magic resistance, build magic resistance first.
Gragas.fight: When Gragas starts drinking with W Drunken Rage, do not unload your damage; wait for the effect to end. Once Gragas E Body Slam is down, if your allies are ready to follow up, root him with Ivern Q Rootcaller and engage together.
Gragas.laning: Pre-mark several camps with Ivern P Friend of the Forest, try to gank lanes while they grow, then return to harvest them.
Gragas.combo: When your ally is ready to follow up, hit Ivern Q Rootcaller, then cast Ivern E Triggerseed on that ally as they engage. Cast Ivern E Triggerseed a little early so its explosion coincides with the root ending, and recast Ivern Q Rootcaller to follow up only when needed. If you summon Ivern R Daisy!, command her to keep attacking the same target and cast Ivern E Triggerseed on Daisy.
Gragas.phase: Gragas has strong burst and formation disruption in the early and mid game, so hold your formation and endure during objective fights at this stage. Gragas's sustained damage falls off in the late game, so Ivern should focus on protecting allied carries and stopping engages.
Gragas.teamfight: Start from behind, root one target with Ivern Q Rootcaller, and let your allies follow up. Cast Ivern E Triggerseed the moment Gragas E Body Slam reaches an allied carry, and place Ivern R Daisy! in front of the carry to stop the engage. Avoid bushes you have no vision of and narrow paths, and do not stand where Gragas R Explosive Cask can knock your allies into the enemy team.
Gragas.escape: Right after you make Gragas use Gragas E Body Slam is Ivern’s chance to close the gap. When allies can follow up, root him with Ivern Q Rootcaller and send Ivern R Daisy! after him. A fleeing Gragas can use Gragas E Body Slam again, so chase only when you can secure the kill.

Hecarim.watch: Hecarim E Devastating Charge deals more damage and knocks back farther the farther he has run, so when Hecarim turns and starts charging, break vision or move toward your allies. If you fight close to Hecarim for too long while W Spirit of Dread is active, he heals based on the amount of damage.
Hecarim.build: Build armor first to prepare for the physical damage from Hecarim Q Rampage and Hecarim E Devastating Charge. Armor cannot block the magic damage from Hecarim W Spirit of Dread or Hecarim R Onslaught of Shadows.
Hecarim.fight: When Hecarim approaches, root him with Ivern Q Rootcaller or hit him with Ivern E Triggerseed's slow to hinder his movement. Hecarim gains attack damage from bonus movement speed, so hindering his movement reduces both his ability to approach and his damage.
Hecarim.laning: Early on, plant seeds at camps with Ivern P Friend of the Forest and try to gank lanes while they grow. When your allies are ready to follow up, hit Ivern Q Rootcaller to help them engage.
Hecarim.combo: When your allies are ready to follow up, root Hecarim with Ivern Q Rootcaller, then cast Ivern E Triggerseed on an ally as they approach. Time the shield's explosion to overlap with the root ending so the slow follows, and recast Ivern Q Rootcaller to engage if needed. If you summon Ivern R Daisy!, command her to keep attacking Hecarim and cast Ivern E Triggerseed on Daisy to aim for an area slow.
Hecarim.escape: When only Hecarim E Devastating Charge is down, Hecarim can escape with R Onslaught of Shadows, so do not rush your engage. Look especially for a chance to close the gap with Ivern Q Rootcaller and send in Ivern R Daisy! before Hecarim R Onslaught of Shadows comes back up.
Hecarim.phase: In the mid and late game, focus on protecting allied carries and stopping Hecarim's engage instead of facing him alone.
Hecarim.teamfight: Start from behind and spread out so your allies are not all hit by Hecarim R Onslaught of Shadows. When Hecarim engages on an allied carry, cast Ivern E Triggerseed and hinder Hecarim's movement with Ivern Q Rootcaller. Place Ivern R Daisy! in front of the carry to stop the engage, and command her to keep attacking Hecarim to aim for the knock-up on her third attack.

JarvanIV.laning: Ivern plants seeds on camps, then tries to gank an allied lane and returns to harvest them while they grow.
JarvanIV.combo: Cast Ivern E Triggerseed a little early so its explosion lines up with the end of the root, and only recast Ivern Q Rootcaller to follow in when needed. If you summon Ivern R Daisy!, command her to keep attacking the same target and cast Ivern E Triggerseed on her.

Karthus.watch: Karthus Q Lay Waste deals more damage when it hits you alone, so walk out of its marked area and stand with an ally when possible. Karthus W Wall of Pain lowers magic resistance and slows, so go around it. After killing Karthus, move straight away from his body to avoid the abilities cast with Karthus P Death Defied.
Karthus.build: Buy a Null-Magic Mantle first in the early game and choose Mercury's Treads for boots. Karthus deals mostly magic damage and Ivern has low magic resistance, so build magic resistance first. However, avoiding Karthus W Wall of Pain and quickly leaving Karthus E Defile's area take priority over building more resistance.
Karthus.fight: Root Karthus, who has no mobility ability, with Ivern Q Rootcaller and cast Ivern E Triggerseed on an ally to help them engage. Don't stay in the marked area of Karthus Q Lay Waste or the area of Karthus E Defile for long while trading damage.
Karthus.laning: Plant bushes on camps with Ivern P Friend of the Forest, then go to a lane and try to gank while they grow.
Karthus.combo: When your allies are ready to follow up, hit with Ivern Q Rootcaller and cast Ivern E Triggerseed on the ally as they engage. Since the shield explodes after a short delay, cast it a little early so its slow continues when the root ends. If needed, recast Ivern Q Rootcaller to follow in, then summon Ivern R Daisy! and command her to keep attacking the same target.
Karthus.escape: Engage when your allies can follow and there is a route that avoids Karthus W Wall of Pain; Karthus has no skill to create distance himself. Root Karthus with Ivern Q Rootcaller and let your allies close in, then send Ivern R Daisy! if needed. After killing Karthus, immediately move away from his body to avoid attacks while Karthus P Death Defied is active.
Karthus.phase: If you miss this window, Karthus will catch up by farming quickly, so overlap camp growth time with your ganking route.
Karthus.teamfight: Start from the back, root one target with Ivern Q Rootcaller, and let your allies close in. Clear the frontline before Karthus can get within Karthus E Defile's range, and protect your allied carry taking damage with Ivern E Triggerseed. Position Ivern R Daisy! in front of your carry, and don't stay near Karthus's body after killing him.

Jax.watch: Jax Q Leap Strike can use a minion or ward as a stepping stone, so watch his engage range. When Jax E Counter Strike is active, stop basic attacking and move outside its stun range. Jax P Relentless Assault grants attack speed, so don't fight him for long.
Jax.build: The provided information does not specify the first item to buy, so one cannot be designated. Consider both the physical damage from Jax Q Leap Strike and the magic damage from Jax W Empower and Jax E Counter Strike; don't lean entirely into one type of resistance. If your allied carry is often caught by crowd control, fit Mikael's Blessing between core items.
Jax.laning: Plant bushes on several camps with Ivern P Friend of the Forest, then gank lanes while they grow. In Jax's lane, hit with Ivern Q Rootcaller when your allies are ready to follow and make use of the root duration. Pressure him with your allies while Jax E Counter Strike is down, and plan your route so you don't encounter Jax alone.
Jax.combo: After dodging the stun from Jax E Counter Strike, hit with Ivern Q Rootcaller and cast Ivern E Triggerseed on an ally as they follow up. Cast Ivern E Triggerseed a little early so it explodes near the end of the root and follows it with a slow. If you summon Ivern R Daisy!, command her to keep attacking Jax and cast Ivern E Triggerseed on Daisy.
Jax.escape: Right after Jax uses Jax Q Leap Strike, take advantage of his lost mobility to root him with Ivern Q Rootcaller and close in with your allies. If Jax E Counter Strike is active, first move out of its stun range, then engage after the stun ends.
Jax.teamfight: Start from the back and protect your allied carry with Ivern E Triggerseed the moment Jax Q Leap Strike reaches them. If Jax engages while Jax E Counter Strike is active, don't group nearby; catch him with Ivern Q Rootcaller and Ivern R Daisy! right after the area stun ends. Position Daisy in front of your carry and command her to keep attacking the same target to look for a knock-up.
Jax.fight: Ivern should avoid extended fights with Jax alone and take short trades near allies. If Jax Q Leap Strike is down, pressure him during that window.
Jax.phase: In the mid and late game, Ivern should protect allied carries and stop Jax from engaging. Don’t try to handle Jax’s side lane pressure alone.

LeeSin.watch: Lee Sin can cross a wall with Lee Sin W Safeguard / Iron Will, so keep your distance from walls when you don’t have vision beyond them.
LeeSin.build: Build armor first against the physical damage from Lee Sin Q Sonic Wave / Resonating Strike and Lee Sin R Dragon's Rage. Armor doesn’t help against the magic damage from Lee Sin E Tempest / Cripple, so don’t expect it to block that damage too.
LeeSin.fight: When Lee Sin Q Sonic Wave / Resonating Strike is on cooldown, land a root and cast Ivern E Triggerseed on an ally so its slow continues as the root wears off.
LeeSin.laning: Early on, avoid routes where you might run into Lee Sin in the jungle and move toward your allies. Use Ivern P Friend of the Forest to seed camps, then gank a lane while they grow and return to harvest them. When ganking, use Ivern Q Rootcaller once your allies are ready to follow.
LeeSin.combo: When allies are ready to engage, land Ivern Q Rootcaller and cast Ivern E Triggerseed on an ally as they follow up. Recast Ivern Q Rootcaller to join if needed. If you’ve summoned Ivern R Daisy!, direct her to keep attacking the same target and cast Ivern E Triggerseed on Daisy.
LeeSin.escape: Before Lee Sin Q Sonic Wave / Resonating Strike comes back up is your chance to close the distance with Ivern Q Rootcaller. Lee Sin can escape if Lee Sin W Safeguard / Iron Will is available, so don’t force an engage just because one mobility ability is on cooldown. Focus your team’s damage together right after Lee Sin uses Lee Sin W Safeguard / Iron Will to engage.
LeeSin.phase: Lee Sin is strong in early duels, so Ivern should avoid fighting him and help allied lanes with early ganks. In the late game, protect allied carries with the lane and objective advantages gained while Lee Sin’s power falls off.
LeeSin.teamfight: Start from the back and catch a target with Ivern Q Rootcaller. Cast Ivern E Triggerseed when Lee Sin engages on an allied carry. Position Ivern R Daisy! in front of the carry to block Lee Sin’s skillshots and disrupt his engage. Keep allies spaced apart just before a team fight so the ally hit by Lee Sin R Dragon's Rage doesn’t collide with them.

Nidalee.watch: Nidalee Q Javelin Toss / Takedown’s spear hurts more the farther away you are when it hits, so dodge when Nidalee throws from range or put your allied frontline between you and her. Avoid Nidalee W Bushwhack / Pounce’s traps too, so you don’t start a fight with a Hunt mark on you. If you’re marked, be ready to use Ivern Q Rootcaller and Ivern R Daisy! when Nidalee leaps in.
Nidalee.build: Early on, buy a Null-Magic Mantle first and choose Mercury's Treads for boots. Nidalee’s main damage is magic, and Ivern tends to have low magic resistance, so build magic resistance first.
Nidalee.fight: Right after Nidalee uses Nidalee W Bushwhack / Pounce to leap, catch her with Ivern Q Rootcaller and help allies engage. Ivern’s main source of magic damage is effective against Nidalee, who tends to have low magic resistance.
Nidalee.laning: Use Ivern P Friend of the Forest to seed camps, then try to gank an allied lane while they grow and return to harvest them. Land Ivern Q Rootcaller when allies are ready to follow, then cast Ivern E Triggerseed as they engage. Watch for Nidalee W Bushwhack / Pounce traps at jungle entrances and in the river, and secure vision first.
Nidalee.combo: When allies are ready to follow, root Nidalee with Ivern Q Rootcaller and cast Ivern E Triggerseed on an ally as they engage. Cast it a little early so the shield’s explosion coincides with the end of the root, then recast Ivern Q Rootcaller to follow if needed. If you’ve summoned Ivern R Daisy!, direct her to keep attacking Nidalee and cast Ivern E Triggerseed on Daisy.
Nidalee.phase: In the mid to late game, focus on protecting allied carries and stopping Nidalee from engaging.
Nidalee.escape: Right after you make Nidalee use Nidalee W Bushwhack / Pounce’s Pounce is your chance to engage. Then, with allies, catch her with Ivern Q Rootcaller and send Ivern R Daisy! after her to stop her escape. Nidalee has no crowd control, so after she uses Pounce, focus on landing Ivern’s root.
Nidalee.teamfight: Start from behind and watch where Nidalee steps out to throw her spear, looking for a chance to catch her with Ivern Q Rootcaller. If Nidalee uses Pounce to dive onto an allied carry, shield them with Ivern E Triggerseed and place Ivern R Daisy! in front of them. Direct Daisy to keep attacking the same target and aim for the knock-up on her third attack.

MasterYi.watch: Master Yi cannot be targeted while casting Master Yi Q Alpha Strike, so root him with Ivern Q Rootcaller as soon as he lands. When Master Yi R Highlander is active, Ivern E Triggerseed's slow has no effect, so protect allies with the shield and stop his engage with a root or Daisy's knockup.
MasterYi.build: Master Yi E Wuju Style's true damage cannot be reduced by resistances, so build health too. Attack speed reduction slows his basic attack damage output and makes Master Yi Q Alpha Strike available less often.
MasterYi.fight: Once Master Yi Q Alpha Strike ends and he lands, root him with Ivern Q Rootcaller, then protect allies with Ivern E Triggerseed as they engage.
MasterYi.laning: Plant bushes at camps with Ivern P Friend of the Forest, gank a lane while they grow, then return to harvest them.
MasterYi.combo: Once Master Yi Q Alpha Strike ends and he lands, hit him with Ivern Q Rootcaller, then cast Ivern E Triggerseed on an ally as they close in. Cast it a little early so the shield burst overlaps with the end of the root, and recast Ivern Q Rootcaller to engage only when needed. If you have summoned Ivern R Daisy!, command her to keep attacking Master Yi and cast Ivern E Triggerseed on Daisy too.
MasterYi.escape: Master Yi Q Alpha Strike is a mobility tool, so immediately after he uses it and lands is your chance to catch him with your allies. Root him with Ivern Q Rootcaller then, and recast it to engage if needed. Don't go in first if your allies aren't ready to follow.
MasterYi.phase: Early on, help your team grow with Ivern’s early ganks while Master Yi’s jungle clear and ganks are weak. Master Yi gets stronger as the game goes on, so in the mid and late game, focus on protecting allied carries and stopping his initial engage.
MasterYi.teamfight: Start from behind and root Master Yi with Ivern Q Rootcaller when you see where Master Yi Q Alpha Strike lands. The moment Master Yi reaches an allied carry, shield them with Ivern E Triggerseed and place Ivern R Daisy! in front of them, directing Daisy to keep attacking the same target. If Master Yi gets his first takedown, he can quickly reach his next target, so group with allies and layer roots and knock-ups.

MonkeyKing.build: Buy armor first against Wukong's main damage and build more armor. Armor won't stop the magic damage from Wukong E Nimbus Strike, and Wukong Q Crushing Blow reduces your armor, so also focus on avoiding his empowered basic attack.
MonkeyKing.fight: When your allies are ready to engage, root Wukong with Ivern Q Rootcaller and take a short trade. Ivern's main magic damage is effective against Wukong's low magic resistance.
MonkeyKing.laning: Plant bushes at camps with Ivern P Friend of the Forest, then move to an allied lane and gank while they grow. When your allies are ready to engage, land Ivern Q Rootcaller and cast Ivern E Triggerseed on the ally closing in. Avoid routes where you could run into the enemy jungler alone, and move toward your allies.
MonkeyKing.combo: After Wukong W Warrior Trickster is down, hit the real Wukong with Ivern Q Rootcaller when your allies are ready to engage. Cast Ivern E Triggerseed on the engaging ally a little early so its slow continues as the root ends, and recast Q to follow if needed. Summon Ivern R Daisy!, command her to keep attacking the same target, and cast E on Daisy to aim for an area slow.
MonkeyKing.phase: In the mid and late game, focus on protecting your carries and stopping Wukong's engage.
MonkeyKing.teamfight: Start from the back, and don't group tightly with allies while Wukong R Cyclone is ready. When Wukong engages on an allied carry, protect them with Ivern E Triggerseed and place Ivern R Daisy! in front of the carry to stop him. Don't mistake the stationary clone from Wukong W Warrior Trickster for the real Wukong; hit the real one with Ivern Q Rootcaller to help your allies engage.
MonkeyKing.escape: After Wukong W Warrior Trickster is down, the window before it returns is a chance to help your team engage with Ivern Q Rootcaller. If Wukong E Nimbus Strike is still available, he can use it to escape, so don’t force an engage just because one mobility ability is down. Right after he uses Wukong R Cyclone as well, fight with your allies or go for an objective.
MonkeyKing.watch: Wukong E Nimbus Strike is a targeted dash, so dodge it from outside its range. After Wukong W Warrior Trickster, don’t use Ivern Q Rootcaller on the stationary clone; watch where the real one will move. Wukong R Cyclone is an area knock-up, and he can recast it and use the clone’s ultimate too, so spread out from allies while it’s available.

Poppy.fight: After Poppy E Heroic Charge is down, catch her with Ivern Q Rootcaller, but wait to use its dash if Poppy W Steadfast Presence is active. Time Ivern E Triggerseed's explosion to overlap with the end of the Q root so its slow continues.
Poppy.laning: Preplant bushes at several jungle camps with Ivern P Friend of the Forest, then gank an allied lane while they grow. Avoid routes where you could run into Poppy, establish vision, and move toward your allies. When ganking, don't put your back to a wall; watch for Poppy E Heroic Charge in open space.
Poppy.combo: After Poppy E Heroic Charge is down and W Steadfast Presence has ended, hit her with Ivern Q Rootcaller when your allies are ready to engage. Cast Ivern E Triggerseed on the engaging ally, and recast Q to go in yourself if needed. Then summon Ivern R Daisy!, command her to keep attacking the same target, and cast E on Daisy to aim for an area slow.
Poppy.phase: In the mid and late game, focus on protecting your carries and stopping Poppy's engage.
Poppy.build: Build armor first against Poppy Q Hammer Shock, E Heroic Charge, and R Keeper’s Verdict. Don’t spend resources on magic resistance just for Poppy. If an allied carry is repeatedly locked down by crowd control, Ivern E Triggerseed can’t free them, so fit Mikael’s Blessing between your core items.
Poppy.escape: Right after you make Poppy use E Heroic Charge is your chance to close the gap with Ivern Q Rootcaller. But if Poppy W Steadfast Presence is active, it blocks Q’s dash, so engage after W ends.
Poppy.teamfight: Start from behind as Ivern, then use Q Rootcaller to catch Poppy or another opponent so your allies can attack them. The moment Poppy E Heroic Charge connects with an allied carry, cast E Triggerseed on them and place R Daisy! in front of the carry. If Poppy charges R Keeper’s Verdict, move out of her line of fire. Once the enemy team is falling apart, put Daisy in their escape route and look for a knock-up.
Poppy.watch: While Poppy W Steadfast Presence is active, don’t use Ivern Q Rootcaller’s dash to engage; wait until it ends. Poppy E Heroic Charge stuns you if it knocks you into a wall, so stay in open space. If Poppy Q Hammer Shock hits you, walk out of its area before the second explosion. When Poppy starts charging R Keeper’s Verdict, move to the side rather than staying in front of her.

Rammus.watch: When you see Rammus rolling in with Q Powerball, put minions between you and him early and keep enough distance to catch him with Ivern Q Rootcaller. Rammus E Frenzying Taunt is targeted, and you can't cast abilities once taunted, so fight from outside its range. Rammus R Soaring Slam has a larger area after he gains speed with Q Powerball, so move well clear and don't stay at the landing point.
Rammus.build: Early on, buy Null-Magic Mantle first and choose Mercury's Treads for boots. Rammus's main damage is magic, and Ivern's magic resistance is relatively low, so build magic resistance first.
Rammus.fight: When Rammus W Defensive Ball Curl is active, stop basic attacking and target someone else or wait; focus your damage with allies after W ends.
Rammus.laning: Plant bushes at several camps with Ivern P Friend of the Forest, then go to a lane and gank while they grow. Avoid angles where you could run into Rammus in the jungle, establish vision, and move toward your allies. When ganking, hit Ivern Q Rootcaller only after your allies are ready to follow.
Rammus.combo: After hitting with Ivern Q Rootcaller, cast Ivern E Triggerseed on an ally as they close in, and recast Q to engage only when needed. Cast E a little early so it bursts around the end of the Q root. If you have summoned Ivern R Daisy!, command her to keep attacking the same target and cast E on Daisy to add a slow.
Rammus.escape: While Rammus R Soaring Slam is down, catch him with Ivern Q Rootcaller and engage with your allies. If Rammus E Frenzying Taunt is still available, stay outside its range; if you're taunted, look for a chance to move with Ivern Q Rootcaller after it ends.
Rammus.phase: In the mid and late game, focus on protecting your carries and stopping Rammus's engage.
Rammus.teamfight: Start from the back and protect an allied carry with Ivern E Triggerseed when Rammus engages on them. Place Ivern R Daisy! in front of the carry to stop his engage, and catch a target for your allies to attack with Ivern Q Rootcaller. While Rammus W Defensive Ball Curl is active, don't focus your basic attacks on him; wait for W to end.

RekSai.watch: Watch for Rek'Sai W Burrow / Un-burrow, which lets her dive underground and knock you up as she emerges. Avoid walls and narrow paths, and move through open areas. When Rek'Sai surfaces, look for a chance to create distance with Ivern Q Rootcaller. Immediately after taking poke from Rek'Sai at range, stay close to allies because Rek'Sai R Void Rush may follow.
RekSai.build: Build armor first to prepare for the physical damage from Rek'Sai Q Queen's Wrath / Prey Seeker and Rek'Sai R Void Rush. Resistance does not reduce the true damage from Rek'Sai E Furious Bite / Tunnel. Rek'Sai R Void Rush scales with your maximum health, so think carefully before stacking health alone.
RekSai.fight: Don't trade damage with Rek'Sai alone; fight where allies can join you. After dodging Rek'Sai W Burrow / Un-burrow's knock-up, root her with Ivern Q Rootcaller. As allies close in, protect them with Ivern E Triggerseed and keep the slow going.
RekSai.laning: Early on, don't cross areas without vision alone; path through the jungle toward your allies. Seed camps, try to gank a lane while they grow, then return to harvest them. Walk over visible Rek'Sai E Furious Bite / Tunnel entrances to destroy them and limit her gank routes.
RekSai.combo: When allies are ready to engage, root Rek'Sai with Ivern Q Rootcaller and shield an ally with Ivern E Triggerseed as they move in. Cast it slightly early so the shield explodes as the root ends, and recast Ivern Q Rootcaller to follow only when needed. Then summon Ivern R Daisy! and direct her to keep attacking Rek'Sai, shielding Daisy with Ivern E Triggerseed.
RekSai.escape: After Rek'Sai W Burrow / Un-burrow misses its knock-up, look for a chance to open an engage for your allies with Ivern Q Rootcaller. If only Rek'Sai E Furious Bite / Tunnel is on cooldown, she can still escape with Rek'Sai R Void Rush, so check for her remaining mobility. Before Rek'Sai R Void Rush is available again, chain your root with the knock-up from Ivern R Daisy! alongside your allies.
RekSai.phase: Avoid giving Rek'Sai early kills and stall for time. In the mid to late game, focus on protecting your allied carry.
RekSai.teamfight: Start from the back and use Ivern Q Rootcaller to stop Rek'Sai's engage or catch a target for your allies to attack. When Rek'Sai reaches an allied carry, shield them with Ivern E Triggerseed and place Ivern R Daisy! in front of them to block her engage. While Rek'Sai is airborne during Rek'Sai R Void Rush, aim Ivern Q Rootcaller at her landing spot.

Nunu.watch: Nunu & Willump W Biggest Snowball Ever! rolls in from far away and knocks you up, so watch for routes that approach from outside your vision. When the snowball comes, walk toward it rather than running in the same direction, then escape along the path Nunu & Willump came from. If hit by Nunu & Willump E Snowball Barrage, move away immediately before its delayed root lands.
Nunu.build: Nunu & Willump's main damage is magic, and Ivern has low magic resistance, so buy Null-Magic Mantle first. Choose Mercury's Treads for both magic resistance and tenacity. If Nunu & Willump Q Consume's healing makes them hard to finish, get Morellonomicon for its healing reduction.
Nunu.fight: After dodging Nunu & Willump W Biggest Snowball Ever!, catch them with Ivern Q Rootcaller and shield the engaging ally with Ivern E Triggerseed. Remember that Nunu & Willump can heal with Nunu & Willump Q Consume, so don't assume a short trade will finish them.
Nunu.laning: Use Ivern P Friend of the Forest to seed camps, then head to a lane with allies and try to gank while the camps grow. Nunu & Willump may return immediately after a gank, so watch for another approach along the same route.
Nunu.combo: When allies are ready to engage, root Nunu & Willump with Ivern Q Rootcaller and shield an ally with Ivern E Triggerseed as they move in. Cast it slightly early so the shield explodes as the root ends, and recast Ivern Q Rootcaller to join the engage when needed. If you summon Ivern R Daisy!, direct her to keep attacking Nunu & Willump and shield Daisy with Ivern E Triggerseed.
Nunu.escape: Engage after dodging Nunu & Willump W Biggest Snowball Ever! and escaping the delayed root from Nunu & Willump E Snowball Barrage. Nunu & Willump has no ability to create distance, so when allies can close in, catch them with Ivern Q Rootcaller and follow up with Ivern R Daisy!.
Nunu.phase: Once you get Ivern R Daisy! in the mid game, your ability to lead fights alongside allies increases. In the late game, stay behind your allies, protect your carry, and stop Nunu & Willump's engage.
Nunu.teamfight: Start from the back and place Ivern R Daisy! between Nunu & Willump and your allied carry. When Nunu & Willump's engage reaches them, shield the carry with Ivern E Triggerseed. When Nunu & Willump R Absolute Zero begins channeling, interrupt it with Ivern Q Rootcaller's root; if you can't interrupt it, move out of range. If Nunu & Willump has already been pushed away, place Daisy on their escape route and have her keep attacking the same target to look for a knock-up.

Rengar.watch: Rengar P Unseen Predator lets him leap from brush and build resource, so when he is out of sight, avoid paths beside brush and secure vision. When his resource bar is full, Rengar E Bola Strike can root you and Rengar W Battle Roar can remove crowd control, so don't start a fight with Ivern Q Rootcaller in that state. When Rengar R Thrill of the Hunt is active, don't roam alone; stay with allies and keep to the back line.
Rengar.build: Build armor first to prepare for Rengar's main damage. Armor can't block the magic damage from Rengar W Battle Roar, and the armor you've built is less effective while Rengar R Thrill of the Hunt reduces it.
Rengar.fight: Once Rengar W Battle Roar is on cooldown, root him with Ivern Q Rootcaller so allies can close in, and time Ivern E Triggerseed so its explosion hits as the root ends. If Rengar's resource bar is full, he can remove crowd control, so don't rush into a trade.
Rengar.laning: Use Ivern P Friend of the Forest to seed several camps in advance. Try to gank an allied lane while they grow, then return to harvest them. During a gank, land Ivern Q Rootcaller when your ally is ready to follow up.
Rengar.combo: Once Rengar W Battle Roar is on cooldown and your allies are ready to close in, root him with Ivern Q Rootcaller. Shield an engaging ally with Ivern E Triggerseed so the slow continues when the root ends, and recast Ivern Q Rootcaller to join when needed. Then summon Ivern R Daisy!, direct her to keep attacking the same target, and shield Daisy with Ivern E Triggerseed.
Rengar.escape: Let Rengar E Bola Strike miss and wait for Rengar W Battle Roar to be used before opening an engage for your allies with Ivern Q Rootcaller.
Rengar.phase: In the late game, focus on protecting your allied carry and stopping Rengar's engage.
Rengar.teamfight: Start from the back, positioning so your allied carry stays behind the frontline and within your vision to prepare for Rengar R Thrill of the Hunt's leap. When Rengar engages and reaches the carry, shield them with Ivern E Triggerseed and place Ivern R Daisy! in front of them to block skillshots. Once Rengar W Battle Roar is on cooldown, catch him with Ivern Q Rootcaller so your allies can attack.

Shyvana.watch: Shyvana R Dragon's Descent is unstoppable during its dash, so don't try to stop it with Ivern Q Rootcaller while she is flying in.
Shyvana.build: Shyvana's main damage is magic, and Ivern has low magic resistance, so build magic resistance first. Buy Null-Magic Mantle early and choose Mercury's Treads for boots.
Shyvana.fight: Pressure Shyvana with your allies early, before she builds stacks of Shyvana P Scalemail. When Shyvana R Dragon's Descent is available, don't engage first. Root Shyvana with Ivern Q Rootcaller after she lands so your allies can control their distance while attacking.
Shyvana.laning: Use Ivern P Friend of the Forest to seed several camps in advance, then gank a lane while they grow. Land Ivern Q Rootcaller when your ally is ready to follow up, and avoid routes where you could meet Shyvana alone in the jungle.
Shyvana.combo: When your allies are ready to engage, root Shyvana with Ivern Q Rootcaller and shield an ally with Ivern E Triggerseed so the slow continues when the root ends. Recast Ivern Q Rootcaller to follow only when needed. If you summon Ivern R Daisy!, direct her to keep attacking Shyvana and shield Daisy with Ivern E Triggerseed.
Shyvana.escape: Save your crowd control while Shyvana engages with Shyvana R Dragon's Descent, and engage after she lands. When Shyvana's Fury bar is empty or her transformation ends and she returns to human form, root her with Ivern Q Rootcaller and pressure her with your allies.
Shyvana.phase: Shyvana has few Shyvana P Scalemail stacks early, so use early ganks to get your allies ahead. In the mid game, help your allies fight alongside Ivern R Daisy!, but don't start an objective if Shyvana's Fury bar is full. In the late game, her permanent stacks put you at a disadvantage, so focus on protecting your allied carry.
Shyvana.teamfight: Start from the back and catch Shyvana with Ivern Q Rootcaller after Shyvana R Dragon's Descent lands. Spread out so your allies aren't hit by the same area-of-effect ability, and shield your carry with Ivern E Triggerseed when Shyvana reaches them. Place Ivern R Daisy! in front of your carry to block her engage and have Daisy keep attacking the same target.

Shaco.build: Build magic resistance first to withstand Shaco's main damage, and buy a Null-Magic Mantle early. Choose Mercury's Treads for boots. Shaco E Two-Shiv Poison deals more damage when you are low on health, so build health as well.
Shaco.fight: Right after Shaco uses Shaco Q Deceive to enter a fight and reveals himself, catch him with Ivern Q Rootcaller so your allies can focus their damage on him. If Shaco uses Shaco R Hallucinate, use health bar reactions to identify the real Shaco and avoid wasting damage on the clone.
Shaco.laning: Early on, maintain vision at your jungle entrances to prepare for Shaco's invades and ganks. Use Ivern P Friend of the Forest to mark several camps in advance, then gank an allied lane while they grow.
Shaco.combo: When Shaco enters with Shaco Q Deceive and reveals himself, root him with Ivern Q Rootcaller, then cast Ivern E Triggerseed on an ally as they move in. If needed, recast Ivern Q Rootcaller to follow up. Cast Ivern E Triggerseed a little early so the shield's explosion overlaps with the end of the root. Then summon Ivern R Daisy! and direct her to keep attacking the same target. Cast Ivern E Triggerseed on Daisy to aim for an area slow.
Shaco.escape: The moment Shaco reveals himself after entering with Shaco Q Deceive is your window to follow up with your allies. Close the distance with Ivern Q Rootcaller and pressure him with Ivern R Daisy! If you have not cleared Shaco W Jack In The Box from a chokepoint without vision, do not enter that area first.
Shaco.phase: Shaco looks for early advantages through ganks and invades, so protect your vision and avoid giving him kills. Buy time by taking objectives; Shaco's ability to fight alone falls off later, and Ivern should focus on protecting allied carries.
Shaco.teamfight: Start from the backline and help your allies focus Shaco by catching him with Ivern Q Rootcaller. When Shaco uses Shaco Q Deceive to reach an allied carry, cast Ivern E Triggerseed on them and place Ivern R Daisy! in front of the carry to block attacks. If you kill Shaco R Hallucinate's clone, move away from it to avoid the explosion and box.
Shaco.watch: Assume Shaco W Jack In The Box is in bushes without vision and around objectives, and clear them ahead of time with Control Wards and Oracle Lens. If Shaco uses Q Deceive to get behind you, his empowered attack is dangerous, so face an ally or keep your back to a wall when you think Shaco is nearby. Shaco R Hallucinate’s clone explodes and leaves a box when it dies, so move away as soon as you kill it.

Sejuani.watch: Sejuani Q Arctic Assault and Sejuani R Glacial Prison are crowd control that can start a fight, so sidestep when you see their windups. If you are hit by the first strike of Sejuani W Winter's Wrath, get out of range before the second strike. Sejuani E Permafrost stacks also build from basic attacks by Sejuani's melee allies, so create distance as the stacks build.
Sejuani.build: Build magic resistance first to withstand Sejuani's main damage, and buy a Null-Magic Mantle early to hold on. Choose Mercury's Treads for boots. If an allied carry is often caught by crowd control, Ivern E Triggerseed cannot remove it, so fit Mikael's Blessing between your core items.
Sejuani.fight: Once Sejuani Q Arctic Assault is down, catch her with Ivern Q Rootcaller to help your allies engage. If Sejuani P Fury of the North has made her immune to slows, damage her first to buy time for her armor to wear off, then use the slow from Ivern E Triggerseed.
Sejuani.laning: Use Ivern P Friend of the Forest to mark several camps, then gank lanes while they grow. Hit Ivern Q Rootcaller when your allies are ready to follow up. Secure vision first and path toward your allies so you do not meet Sejuani alone in the jungle.
Sejuani.escape: Right after Sejuani's mobility tool, Sejuani Q Arctic Assault, is down, you have a window to catch her with Ivern Q Rootcaller and engage with your allies. After Sejuani E Permafrost stuns a target, there is a short window during which stacks do not build on that target again. However, Sejuani's first basic attack immediately after the stun deals bonus damage based on the target's maximum health, so have the affected ally create distance first.
Sejuani.teamfight: Start from the backline and catch Sejuani or another enemy with Ivern Q Rootcaller so your allies can engage on them. When Sejuani uses Sejuani Q Arctic Assault or Sejuani R Glacial Prison to engage on an allied carry, protect them with Ivern E Triggerseed. Place Daisy, summoned with Ivern R Daisy!, in front of the carry to block skillshots, and direct her to keep attacking one target to try to knock them up.
Sejuani.combo: Once Sejuani Q Arctic Assault is down and your allies are ready to follow up, hit her with Ivern Q Rootcaller. While your allies engage, cast Ivern E Triggerseed on an ally so its slow follows as the root ends, then recast Ivern Q Rootcaller to join if needed. Next, summon Ivern R Daisy! and have her keep attacking the same target; cast Ivern E Triggerseed on Daisy to aim for an area slow.
Sejuani.phase: As Sejuani gets tankier over time, focus on protecting your allied carry and stopping engages as Ivern.

Taliyah.watch: Taliyah Q Threaded Volley cannot change direction while being cast, so sidestep instead of retreating in a straight line.
Taliyah.build: Early on, withstand Taliyah's magic damage with a Null-Magic Mantle and choose Mercury's Treads for boots. Ivern has low magic resistance, so build it first.
Taliyah.fight: Using Ivern Q Rootcaller's dash into an area covered by Taliyah E Unraveled Earth can stun you, so avoid the rock field when engaging. When your allies are ready to follow up, root Taliyah with Ivern Q Rootcaller, then chain your allies' attacks with Ivern E Triggerseed.
Taliyah.laning: Use Ivern P Friend of the Forest to mark several camps, then gank a lane while they grow before returning to harvest them. If Taliyah disappears from the jungle, she can quickly intervene in another lane, so have your allies back off in advance.
Taliyah.escape: Do not engage just because either Taliyah E Unraveled Earth or Taliyah R Weaver's Wall is down. In particular, before Taliyah R Weaver's Wall comes back, close the distance with Ivern Q Rootcaller and send in Ivern R Daisy! when you can avoid the rock field on the ground.
Taliyah.phase: In the mid to late game, watch for Taliyah's fast rotations to other lanes while keeping allied carries alive and stopping engages.
Taliyah.teamfight: Start from the backline and root Taliyah with Ivern Q Rootcaller so your allies can follow up. Cast Ivern E Triggerseed the moment Taliyah's engage reaches an allied carry. Place Ivern R Daisy! in front of the carry to block skillshots, then position her in the enemy's escape path to try to knock them up as the enemy team collapses. If the enemy's crowd control often catches your allied carry, fit Mikael's Blessing between your core items.
Taliyah.combo: When your allies are ready to follow up, hit an enemy with Ivern Q Rootcaller and cast Ivern E Triggerseed on an ally so its explosion and slow follow as the root ends. If Taliyah E Unraveled Earth isn’t on the ground where you plan to engage, recast Ivern Q Rootcaller when needed. Summon Ivern R Daisy!, order her to keep attacking the same target, then cast Ivern E Triggerseed on Daisy.

Skarner.watch: Skarner E Ixtal's Impact dashes through terrain, and he stuns you if you hit a wall after being grabbed. Do not let a wall be behind you; move into open space, and stay alert for his next dash if you hit a wall. Skarner R Impale suppresses you and cannot be escaped with Ivern Q Rootcaller's movement or stun, so stay out of its range.
Skarner.build: Buy a Null-Magic Mantle first early on, and choose Mercury's Treads for boots. Skarner deals mostly magic damage and Ivern has low magic resistance, so build magic resistance first. If the enemy team has a lot of crowd control that can lock down an allied carry, fit Mikael's Blessing between your core items.
Skarner.fight: When Skarner gets close, he builds damage with empowered basic attacks from Skarner Q Shattered Earth/Upheaval, so fight outside his melee range. Once Skarner E Ixtal's Impact is down, root him with Ivern Q Rootcaller and cast Ivern E Triggerseed on an ally as they move in. Start the fight when your allies are ready to engage.
Skarner.laning: Use Ivern P Friend of the Forest to mark several camps in advance, then gank allied lanes while they grow. Save your Smite charges instead of using them on camps when preparing for Dragon or Herald.
Skarner.combo: After Skarner E Ixtal's Impact is down, hit him with Ivern Q Rootcaller to root him and let your allies follow up. Cast Ivern E Triggerseed on an ally a little early so the slow follows when the root ends, and recast Ivern Q Rootcaller to engage if needed. If you summon Ivern R Daisy!, direct her to keep attacking the same target and cast Ivern E Triggerseed on Daisy.
Skarner.escape: The moment Skarner E Ixtal's Impact is down is your window to close the distance with Ivern Q Rootcaller. Send in Ivern R Daisy! then and direct her to keep attacking the same target. If Skarner R Impale is still available, watch its suppression range and do not lead the engage yourself as Ivern.
Skarner.phase: Skarner's damage increases as he builds tank items, so delay that point with early pressure and objectives, then focus on protecting allied carries in the mid to late game.
Skarner.teamfight: Start from the backline and catch Skarner or another enemy with Ivern Q Rootcaller. Cast Ivern E Triggerseed when Skarner engages on an allied carry. Place Ivern R Daisy! in front of the carry to block skillshots, and direct her to keep attacking the same target to try to knock them up. Do not stand against the wall at the edge of the Dragon or Baron pit, as Skarner R Impale can pull you in.

Vi.watch: When Vi charges Q Vault Breaker, dodge by moving backward or to the side. Vi W Denting Blows gets more dangerous the longer she hits the same target, so don’t trade with her for long. Vi R Cease and Desist chases its target to the end, so don’t let your allied carry wander out of vision alone.
Vi.build: Build armor first against Vi’s main damage. Vi W Denting Blows deals damage based on maximum health, so avoid stacking health alone. If there is a lot of crowd control that can lock down your allied carry, Ivern E Triggerseed can’t free them, so fit Mikael’s Blessing between your core items.
Vi.fight: Right after dodging Vi Q Vault Breaker, root her with Ivern Q Rootcaller to give your allies a chance to follow up. If Vi is charging in with R Cease and Desist, don’t try to displace her; respond after she lands and the knockup ends.
Vi.laning: Plant brush in jungle camps with Ivern P Friend of the Forest, then visit a lane to gank while they grow and return to harvest them. Land Ivern Q Rootcaller when your allies are ready to follow up. If Vi’s shield is active, trade after it has been removed.
Vi.combo: Once Vi Q Vault Breaker is down and your allies are ready to follow up, root her with Ivern Q Rootcaller. While your allies charge in, cast Ivern E Triggerseed on one of them so its slow follows as the root ends. Recast Ivern Q Rootcaller to join if needed, and summon Ivern R Daisy! and direct her to keep attacking the same target.
Vi.escape: The moment to engage is right after you bait out and dodge Vi Q Vault Breaker. When your allies can go in with you, close the distance with Ivern Q Rootcaller and chase with Ivern R Daisy! If Vi R Cease and Desist is in progress, wait until she lands and the knockup ends.
Vi.phase: In the mid to late game, focus on protecting your allied carry and stopping Vi’s engage.
Vi.teamfight: Start from behind your team and protect your allied carry with Ivern E Triggerseed when Vi Q Vault Breaker or Vi R Cease and Desist reaches them. Put Ivern R Daisy! in front of your carry to block non-targeted abilities, and use Ivern Q Rootcaller to catch the target your allies should attack. If Vi is charging in with R Cease and Desist, save your displacement and respond after she lands.

Udyr.watch: Watch for the stun on Udyr’s first attack when he approaches with E Blazing Stampede. Immobilizing effects don’t work while Udyr E Blazing Stampede is awakened, so catch him with Ivern Q Rootcaller after the awakening ends. Udyr Q Wilding Claw and Udyr R Wingborne Storm deal damage based on maximum health, so don’t stay close and fight for long.
Udyr.build: Build armor items first against Udyr’s physical damage. Armor won’t block the magic damage from Udyr R Wingborne Storm, and Udyr Q Wilding Claw deals mixed damage, so consider magic resistance too. Since he has damage based on maximum health, avoid stacking health alone.
Udyr.fight: Once Udyr W Iron Mantle’s shield is gone and he has used the stun from Udyr E Blazing Stampede, you have a chance to press the attack with your allies. Catch him with Ivern Q Rootcaller to let your allies engage, and protect an ally with Ivern E Triggerseed.
Udyr.laning: Use vision at jungle entrances and key paths to track Udyr, and keep your allied lanes from pushing forward when he’s out of sight. Ivern plants seeds in camps, visits allied lanes to gank while they grow, then returns to harvest the camps. Avoid routes where you might meet Udyr alone, and use Ivern Q Rootcaller when your allies are ready to follow up.
Udyr.combo: After Udyr E Blazing Stampede’s awakening ends and its stun is used, land Ivern Q Rootcaller when your allies are ready to engage. While they follow up, cast Ivern E Triggerseed so its slow continues as the root ends, and recast Ivern Q Rootcaller to engage if needed. If the fight continues, summon Ivern R Daisy!, direct her to keep attacking the same target, and cast Ivern E Triggerseed on Daisy.
Udyr.phase: In the mid to late game, focus on protecting your allied carry and stopping Udyr’s engage.
Udyr.teamfight: Ivern should start from behind and cast Ivern E Triggerseed when Udyr reaches an allied carry. Put Ivern R Daisy! in front of the carry to stop his engage, and catch Udyr with Ivern Q Rootcaller once Udyr E Blazing Stampede’s awakening ends. Rather than trying to take down Udyr first while he also has Udyr W Iron Mantle’s shield, deal with the weak enemies behind him with your allies, then face him with a numbers advantage.
Udyr.escape: If Udyr has already used his stun by approaching with E Blazing Stampede, create distance or counterattack with your allies while he can’t immediately stun the same target again. After Udyr E Blazing Stampede’s awakening ends, catch him with Ivern Q Rootcaller. Right after you make Udyr use E Blazing Stampede, look for a chance to pick him off with Ivern R Daisy!. Don’t rely solely on walking to escape Udyr; save Ivern Q Rootcaller.

Viego.watch: Viego W Spectral Maw’s stun lasts longer the more he charges it, so dodge to the side when you see him charging and interrupt it with Ivern Q Rootcaller if possible. If you see black mist over terrain, watch for Viego to approach through E Harrowed Path and avoid that route. When your health is low, fall back because you’re an easy target for Viego R Heartbreaker.
Viego.build: Build armor first against the physical damage from Viego Q Blade of The Ruined King and Viego R Heartbreaker. If a long fight is unavoidable, consider anti-heal next to counter healing from Viego P Sovereign’s Domination and Viego Q Blade of The Ruined King. If the stun from Viego W Spectral Maw keeps your allied carry locked down, fit Mikael’s Blessing between your core items.
Viego.fight: If an ally falls, root Viego with Ivern Q Rootcaller so he can’t interact with the wraith left there, then create distance from the spot.
Viego.laning: Early on, plant seeds in camps, then visit a lane to gank while they grow and return to harvest them. Avoid angles where you could meet Viego in the jungle, secure vision first, and path toward your allies. Don’t push a lane in the direction of black mist created by Viego E Harrowed Path; take a route around it.
Viego.combo: Land Ivern Q Rootcaller when your allies are ready to follow up, then cast Ivern E Triggerseed on an ally as they charge in. Cast Ivern E Triggerseed a little early so the shield explodes and its slow continues as the root ends. If you need to hinder Viego’s escape further, summon Ivern R Daisy!, direct her to keep attacking the same target, and cast Ivern E Triggerseed on Daisy.
Viego.escape: Don’t go in just because Viego W Spectral Maw is down. Wait until Viego R Heartbreaker is also unavailable and your allies can engage together, then root him with Ivern Q Rootcaller and send Ivern R Daisy! after him.
Viego.phase: In the mid to late game, focus on protecting your allied carry and denying Viego kills.
Viego.teamfight: Ivern should start from behind and use Ivern Q Rootcaller to root Viego or catch the target your allies should attack. If Viego engages on an allied carry, protect them with Ivern E Triggerseed and put Ivern R Daisy! in front of them. Where an ally has fallen, root Viego so he can’t interact with the wraith; if Viego has possessed a body, create distance and look for the moment he returns to his original body.

Warwick.watch: When health drops below half, Warwick W Blood Hunt reveals the position and increases Warwick’s movement and attack speed, so don’t remain in the jungle or a lane after losing health. When Warwick E Primal Howl is active, back away because it reduces incoming damage and is followed by a fear. Warwick R Infinite Duress can engage and suppress you from long range, so don’t consider a brush without vision or the other side of a wall a safe distance away.
Warwick.build: Buy Null-Magic Mantle first and choose Mercury’s Treads for boots. Prioritize magic resistance against damage from Warwick P Eternal Hunger, Warwick Q Jaws of the Beast, and Warwick R Infinite Duress. Armor against his basic attack physical damage is also valuable, and if healing becomes a problem in a long fight, consider anti-heal after resistances.
Warwick.fight: Don’t commit your damage while Warwick E Primal Howl is active; catch him with Ivern Q Rootcaller after the fear. Engage with your allies while Warwick R Infinite Duress is down and pressure him with Ivern R Daisy!
Warwick.laning: Plant seeds in several camps with Ivern P Friend of the Forest, then try to gank a lane while they grow. Land Ivern Q Rootcaller when your allies are ready to follow up immediately, and use the root duration. If health falls below half, recall even if you have to give up some farming, mindful of Warwick W Blood Hunt.
Warwick.combo: When your allies are ready to follow up, land Ivern Q Rootcaller, then cast Ivern E Triggerseed on an ally as they engage. Use Ivern E Triggerseed a little early so its explosion coincides with the end of the root, and recast Ivern Q Rootcaller to engage yourself only when needed. If you’ve summoned Ivern R Daisy!, direct her to attack the same target and cast Ivern E Triggerseed on Daisy to aim for an area slow and a knockup on her third attack.
Warwick.escape: Don’t rush in when only Warwick Q Jaws of the Beast is down; Warwick can still escape with R Infinite Duress. Once Warwick R Infinite Duress is down and the fear from Warwick E Primal Howl has also been used, close the distance with Ivern Q Rootcaller alongside your allies and send Ivern R Daisy! after him.
Warwick.phase: In the mid to late game, focus on protecting your allied carry and stopping Warwick’s engage.
Warwick.teamfight: Start from behind, catch Warwick with Ivern Q Rootcaller, and create an opening for your allies to attack. If Warwick engages on an allied carry, protect them with Ivern E Triggerseed and pressure him by putting Ivern R Daisy! in front of the carry. If Warwick R Infinite Duress suppresses an ally, focus on saving them and concentrate your counterattack while Warwick is locked in place.

XinZhao.watch: Dodge the follow-up thrust from Xin Zhao W Wind Becomes Lightning by moving sideways. If you’ve been hit twice by the empowered attacks from Xin Zhao Q Three Talon Strike, get out of range before the third hit knocks you up. While Xin Zhao R Crescent Guard is active, don’t try to deal damage from outside his spear range; back away and wait for it to expire.
XinZhao.build: Build armor first to defend against Xin Zhao’s main damage. Armor can’t block the magic damage from Xin Zhao E Audacious Charge, and Xin Zhao R Crescent Guard adds damage based on your current health, so avoid relying on a large health increase alone.
XinZhao.fight: Once Xin Zhao E Audacious Charge is down, root him with Ivern Q Rootcaller and shield the ally going in with Ivern E Triggerseed. If Xin Zhao R Crescent Guard is active, back away and counterattack after it ends.
XinZhao.laning: Early on, use Ivern P Friend of the Forest to plant groves at camps. While they grow, visit lanes and look for ganks. Avoid routes where you could meet the enemy jungler alone, establish vision first, and move toward your allies.
XinZhao.combo: Once Xin Zhao E Audacious Charge is down and your ally is ready to engage, root him with Ivern Q Rootcaller. Shield your ally with Ivern E Triggerseed as they go in, timing the explosion so its slow follows as the root ends. If needed, recast Ivern Q Rootcaller to join the fight, then summon Ivern R Daisy! and direct her to keep attacking the same target.
XinZhao.escape: The window to catch Xin Zhao with Ivern Q Rootcaller is right after you bait out Xin Zhao E Audacious Charge. Dodge the third hit of Xin Zhao Q Three Talon Strike, then go in with your ally.
XinZhao.phase: In the mid to late game, protect your allied carry and look for a counterattack as soon as Xin Zhao R Crescent Guard ends.
XinZhao.teamfight: Start from the back and prepare for Xin Zhao’s engage. The moment he reaches your allied carry, shield them with Ivern E Triggerseed and place Ivern R Daisy! in front of them to block his approach. Keep some distance from your allies so Xin Zhao R Crescent Guard’s knockback doesn’t split your formation. When its duration ends, catch him with Ivern Q Rootcaller and counterattack.

Zac.watch: Zac E Elastic Slingshot has a visible charge-up, and getting hit lets him engage with a knock-up. If you see him charging behind a wall, interrupt him with Ivern Q Rootcaller and move out of the landing area. Keep your distance so you don’t take repeated damage from Zac W Unstable Matter, which deals damage based on your maximum health.
Zac.build: Early on, buy a Null-Magic Mantle first and choose Mercury’s Treads for your boots. Zac deals mostly magic damage, and Ivern has relatively low magic resistance, so build magic resistance first.
Zac.fight: Right after baiting out Zac E Elastic Slingshot, root him with Ivern Q Rootcaller to give your ally a chance to engage. During the fight, step on the blobs dropped by Zac P Cell Division to prevent him from healing.
Zac.laning: Plant seeds at camps, then visit lanes and try to gank with Ivern Q Rootcaller while they grow; return to harvest them afterward. Avoid angles where you could meet Zac, establish vision first, then route toward a lane with an ally. Land Ivern Q Rootcaller when your ally is ready to engage.
Zac.combo: If you see Zac E Elastic Slingshot charging, interrupt it with Ivern Q Rootcaller. After Zac’s engage is down, hit him with Ivern Q Rootcaller, then shield the ally going in with Ivern E Triggerseed so its slow follows as the root ends. If needed, recast Ivern Q Rootcaller to engage, then summon Ivern R Daisy! and direct her to keep attacking the same target.
Zac.escape: The window for Ivern to go in is right after you bait out Zac E Elastic Slingshot. If your ally is ready to engage, root Zac with Ivern Q Rootcaller, and only recast it when you need to close the distance. At that point, send Ivern R Daisy! in to attack the same target.
Zac.phase: In the late game, focus on saving your allied carry and stopping Zac’s engage.
Zac.teamfight: Start from the back. If you see Zac E Elastic Slingshot charging, interrupt it with Ivern Q Rootcaller. When Zac engages on your allied carry, shield them with Ivern E Triggerseed and place Ivern R Daisy! in front of them. After weathering his engage, back away to avoid damage from Zac W Unstable Matter, and step on the blobs dropped by Zac P Cell Division to destroy them.

Belveth.watch: Bel'Veth W Above and Below chains into a chase with a knock-up and slow, so if she gets close, dodge by turning sideways instead of running straight back. Bel'Veth takes greatly reduced damage while Bel'Veth E Royal Maelstrom is active, so don’t time the explosion from Ivern E Triggerseed to hit during it. Bel'Veth R Endless Banquet heals and deals true damage based on missing health, so be especially careful at low health.
Belveth.build: Build armor first to account for the damage from Bel'Veth Q Void Surge and Bel'Veth E Royal Maelstrom. Armor can’t block the magic damage from Bel'Veth W Above and Below, and resistances can’t reduce the true damage from Bel'Veth R Endless Banquet, so also build up your total health.
Belveth.fight: If Bel'Veth dashes in with Bel'Veth Q Void Surge and you dodge Bel'Veth W Above and Below, root her with Ivern Q Rootcaller to help your ally engage. Deal burst damage after Bel'Veth E Royal Maelstrom ends.
Belveth.laning: Early on, use Ivern P Friend of the Forest to plant seeds at camps, then visit lanes and try to gank with Ivern Q Rootcaller while they grow. If dragon or Rift Herald is coming up, save Smite instead of using it to harvest a camp immediately.
Belveth.combo: When your ally is ready to engage, hit Bel'Veth with Ivern Q Rootcaller and cast Ivern E Triggerseed on that ally as they go in. Time the shield explosion to go off as the root ends, and recast Ivern Q Rootcaller to join if needed. If you’ve summoned Ivern R Daisy!, direct her to keep attacking Bel'Veth and cast Ivern E Triggerseed on Daisy to aim for an area slow.
Belveth.escape: Dodge Bel'Veth W Above and Below sideways, then engage after checking which direction Bel'Veth Q Void Surge was used in. Bel'Veth Q Void Surge has a separate cooldown for each direction, but she may still have mobility options available, so chain Ivern Q Rootcaller’s root with Ivern R Daisy!’s knock-up alongside your ally.
Belveth.phase: Bel'Veth becomes harder to deal with over time because of her permanent stacks, so in the mid to late game, focus on protecting your allied carry and stopping her engage.
Belveth.teamfight: Start from the back and catch Bel'Veth with Ivern Q Rootcaller. When she reaches your allied carry, cast Ivern E Triggerseed on them. Place Ivern R Daisy! in front of your carry to block her engage, and direct Daisy to keep attacking the same target to aim for a knock-up on her third attack. If an ally falls and a Void Coral appears, retreat before Bel'Veth picks it up. Delay the team fight while Bel'Veth R Endless Banquet’s transformation is active.

Nocturne.watch: If Nocturne Q Duskbringer hits you, he can quickly close in along its trail, so don’t run straight away; angle toward an ally or turret. If Nocturne E Unspeakable Horror connects, create distance to break the tether before the fear triggers. Don’t rush to use Ivern Q Rootcaller while Nocturne W Shroud of Darkness is active. If Nocturne R Paranoia darkens your screen, move toward your allies immediately.
Nocturne.build: Nocturne’s main damage is physical, so build armor first. Armor can’t block the magic damage from Nocturne E Unspeakable Horror, but the information provided isn’t enough to recommend a specific item.
Nocturne.fight: If Nocturne W Shroud of Darkness is still available, delay Ivern Q Rootcaller so it doesn’t get blocked.
Nocturne.laning: Use Ivern P Friend of the Forest to plant groves at several camps, then visit lanes and look for ganks while they grow. Avoid routes where you could meet Nocturne alone in the jungle, establish vision around the river and jungle entrances, then move toward your allies. Land Ivern Q Rootcaller to help your ally engage when they’re ready.
Nocturne.combo: After confirming Nocturne W Shroud of Darkness is down, root him with Ivern Q Rootcaller and cast Ivern E Triggerseed on the ally going in. Use it slightly early so the shield explodes as the root ends and its slow follows. If needed, recast Ivern Q Rootcaller to engage, then summon Ivern R Daisy! and direct her to keep attacking the same target.
Nocturne.escape: While Nocturne R Paranoia is down, look for a chance to open an engage for your ally with Ivern Q Rootcaller. Keep a way to create distance ready for when Nocturne casts Nocturne E Unspeakable Horror, then fight alongside your ally again once the tether breaks.
Nocturne.phase: In the mid to late game, focus on protecting your allied carry and stopping Nocturne’s engage.
Nocturne.teamfight: Start team fights from the back, and when Nocturne R Paranoia is active, move toward your allies instead of splitting up. When Nocturne engages on your allied carry, cast Ivern E Triggerseed on them and place Ivern R Daisy! in front of them. After Nocturne W Shroud of Darkness is down, catch him with Ivern Q Rootcaller so your allies can attack together.
